g.text: Distributed Locks: the expiry race, and why the fencing token is the real fix
Process A stalls past the TTL; Process B takes over; the resource decides who wins, not the lock
The lock alone can't stop this: by the time A resumes, it has no way to know its lock expired.
The fencing token does -- the resource remembers the highest token it has ever accepted (2) and
rejects any write carrying a lower one. Correctness lives at the resource, not the lock.
